name: portkeeper
description: See the ports you have open and who started them. A tiny menu bar / tray widget for macOS and Windows.

paragraphs: Not verified by Apple or Microsoft yet. Portkeeper has no developer certificate for now, so macOS and Windows show a one-time warning when you first open it. That is expected and the app is safe: every build comes from the public code in this repository through GitHub Actions. Two clicks get past the warning (see Install), or use the one-command install below, which shows no dialog at all. The warning disappears once the app is notarized.

Portkeeper puts that in one small panel in your menu bar (macOS) or system tray (Windows): every project with a listening port, grouped by folder, with the logo of the agent or IDE that started it. Click a port to open it. Stop it with one click. Start it again later. Lock the ones a client depends on so nobody stops them by mistake.

requirements.text: Appearance (Glass on macOS: Liquid Glass on macOS 26, the system blur before; opaque Dark or Light everywhere, with native rounded corners on Windows 11), language (English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese), launch at login, open on start, show all processes, check for updates.
